faq.defaultModel.q: What changes when I pick a default model?
faq.defaultModel.a: The default model is the one your AI helper and your Bots use unless told otherwise. A new default for AI helper and tasks switches your AI helper and tasks; a new default for Bots switches the Bots that follow the default. Bots and agents that have their own model keep it. If the new model is paid for with your own key, its use is billed to that provider account.
faq.keyKept.q: Where is my key kept, and can I see it again?
faq.keyKept.a: A key is stored only on the computer you connect it on, and is never shown again. Check and save asks for a check first; if the provider refuses it, nothing is saved. If the check can't finish, or this computer can't check keys, the key is saved and shown as not checked when that result comes back. If the answer is lost, the page can confirm the save by its fingerprint and may call it confirmed without a check. Removing an account stops anything using it, and nothing switches to another AI by itself. Spending shows the total this computer recorded; your provider's own bill is the final word.
faq.claudeCode.q: Can I use my own Claude plan?
faq.claudeCode.a: Yes, through Claude Code on this computer. If it is not installed or not signed in, the page can open a terminal on the computer and run the command for you; to sign in, follow the link it shows. The page checks Claude Code again on its own while the step runs. Once you turn it on, new chats on this computer use your Claude plan. You can also copy Claude Code's sign-in from a computer where it works to another computer of this realm: the file is copied as it is, readable only by its owner, and you see what changes before anything is written.
faq.agents.q: What is an agent, and what does its tool list do?
faq.agents.a: Agents are the definitions chats and helpers run on; new chats start on the default one. An agent Hoody owns is read-only except for its model. With strict off, the tool list is a base and Hoody adds what the agent needs. An agent with no tool list gets Hoody's default tools if it is strict, and otherwise every tool, also ones added later. Ticking tools replaces that with exactly the ticked ones; unticking one of every tool saves a list of the others. To give an agent no tools, turn strict on in its file first.
faq.skillTrust.q: What is the difference between turning a skill on and trusting it?
faq.skillTrust.a: Turning a skill on lets every agent in this realm load it; it does not change trust. A skill you install or import starts off and not trusted. While it is on but not trusted, agents see its name only: its description and instructions are withheld and its commands do not run. Its commands run only after you trust it, and then they run on this computer, as you, each time it loads.
faq.instructionsMemory.q: What do instructions and memory add to my agents?
faq.instructionsMemory.a: Instructions are text that is added whenever an agent's instructions are built, unless the chat's or agent's prompt settings leave it out. A chat picks up a change at its next turn; a helper or workflow step already running keeps the version it started with. Memory is what agents learned while working; they recall it when it fits the task. The memory switch turns it on or off for every agent in the realm on that computer, and what is stored stays.
faq.autoKinds.q: What are loops, TODOs and workflows?
faq.autoKinds.a: A loop repeats a prompt inside one chat on a timer. It runs while that chat is open on the computer and is lost if the agent restarts; at most 8 run on a computer, counted over every realm. For something that must keep happening, use Schedules or a TODO. TODOs are work the agent keeps for later: you or an agent files it, triage sorts it, and a worker can run it. Workflows lists each workflow's step count; select one to see its steps and inputs, and its timeout if it has one. Saving a shipped one makes your own changed copy, and Reset to shipped brings the shipped version back.
faq.workflowRuns.q: What happens to a workflow while it runs?
faq.workflowRuns.a: A workflow's runs show under it, and All runs lists them all. The agent closes a chat that nobody has open a few minutes after it goes idle, and a chat waiting for your answer counts as idle. While this page is open, the Hub keeps the chats of up to 8 running workflows open; any more are not kept, and none are once the page is closed.
faq.rulesHooks.q: What do rules and hooks do, and what is a settings chat?
faq.rulesHooks.a: Rules are what the agent follows in every chat. A limit or a check-in is judged by the safety checker before a tool call runs; guidance and playbooks are advice the agent reads. Hooks are commands that run on this computer, as you, when something happens in a chat, such as before a tool runs or when a chat ends. Rules are read with nothing open; your first rules change and your hooks use a settings chat: no tools, kept open while you are on the page, closed when you leave.
faq.connections.q: What do the GitHub and MCP connections give my agents?
faq.connections.a: A linked GitHub account is what the agent on this computer uses to clone, commit and push; its tokens stay on the computer and are never shown. MCP servers are tool servers agents on the computer can call: a command server runs on the computer, an address server receives your agents' tool calls. Agents see a server's tools as name__tool. Values you save for a server stay on the computer and are never shown again; to change one, type a new value.
faq.settle.q: Why does a chat say Settle it first?
faq.settle.a: When a rename, close, delete or Remove what follows on a chat loses its answer, the Hub can't tell whether it went through, so it never sends it again. Open the same action again (Rename, Close chat or Delete chat in the chat's menu, or Remove what follows in a reply's menu) and press Check again: it reads the chat and shows what it finds. Until that change is settled, the other three can't start on that chat, so two of them never cross. Sending messages still works.
faq.autoRun.q: What happens when I run or approve a TODO?
faq.autoRun.a: Run and Approve start a worker on this computer that works on the TODO on its own: nobody is asked anything, so its questions and approval requests are denied. It spends model budget. While a worker holds the TODO, it is not started again and its proposed runs wait until that run ends; you can cancel the run. When the worker is done, the TODO moves to review. If the agent refuses, nothing starts: another worker may hold the TODO, or this computer already runs as many as it allows. A proposal decided otherwise meanwhile changes nothing.
faq.autoCancel.q: What does cancelling a TODO run do?
faq.autoCancel.a: The worker stops and the TODO goes back to ready; what it already changed stays. Once the agent takes the cancel, the page reads how that run ended. A run that had already finished moved to review. When the TODO shows that a run ended but does not say which, that end may not be this run's, so it is never shown as this cancel's outcome. If no run is going when you confirm, nothing is sent.
faq.autoUnsure.q: Why does it say this may have gone through?
faq.autoUnsure.a: When the answer to a run, approval, cancel or loop change is lost, the Hub can't tell whether it went through, so it never sends it again. Check again only reads the TODO or the chat's loops; it never starts another. A change it does not show yet may still be on its way. Some can never be proved by a read: a worker start the TODO shows may be this run or another, and a loop's run count or end time can't show which request changed it. For a lost new loop it lists look-alikes started since you sent it; an empty list does not prove none started.
faq.autoNotSent.q: Why does it say nothing was sent?
faq.autoNotSent.a: Right before sending, the page reads the TODO or the chat's loops again. If that read fails, if the action is no longer offered, or if what the confirm applies to changed (another run holds the TODO, the proposal was decided, the TODO was edited, the loop is gone), nothing is sent. Review it and try again. While the TODO or loop can't be read, the confirm button stays off.
faq.loopChange.q: How do pausing, changing and deleting a loop work?
faq.loopChange.a: A paused loop no longer keeps its chat open: if nobody has it open, the agent may close it, ending the loop. A missing loop may have ended with its chat. Delete stops and removes it; its chat and what earlier runs wrote stay. A timing change stops the loop, then starts a new one in the same chat once the old one is gone. If the stop's answer was lost or the new one is not started, nothing new runs until you choose to start it. A new loop is refused when its chat is closed or the computer already runs 8. An expired loop restarts with a new end time; an end before its first run is not taken.
faq.forkUnconfirmed.q: Why is a fork not confirmed, and what can I do?
faq.forkUnconfirmed.a: When a fork's answer is lost, the Hub can't tell if the chat was made. It keeps the fork as unconfirmed and never sends it again; Fork on that reply checks it. Check again doesn't send another fork. If it finds the new chat, it opens it when it can; if none was made and Check can block a late one and record that, it frees the reply. If the fork ended with no chat to open here and Check can record that, it frees the reply, but the chat may exist: see your chat list. Otherwise the row stays. Hide only hides the row; the fork still holds its reply. At most 8 forks per account wait like this.
faq.strictApprovals.q: What does Ask every time ask about, and what does it turn off?
faq.strictApprovals.a: Asks before every command, file change or delete, changing web request, computer action, MCP tool that is not read-only, image or notification. Reading, searching and tasks never ask; saving memory and TODO edits do not ask. Helpers, workflow runs, the orchestrator, other CLIs, TODO runs and hook tests are off; your hooks are skipped; MCP servers do not start.
